english.title: Lock on to person / object / land to cause serious disruption
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, attached

(A)_[yourself to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY OTHER PERSON..),]_
(B)_[yourself to an object, namely **(..SPECIFY OBJECT..),]_
(C)_[yourself to land at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..),]_

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 34 for the meaning of 'serious disruption'.
(ii) For the purpose of the offence, a dwelling is a building or structure which is used as a dwelling or, a part of a building or structure, if the part is used as a dwelling including any yard, garden, grounds, garage or outhouse belonging to and used with a dwelling (section 1(5)).
(iii) It is a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove that they had a reasonable excuse for the act that caused or was capable of causing serious disruption (section 1(2)).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum term of imprisonment for summary offences and/or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

Note
The maximum term for summary offences is 6 months where the offence is committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 is in force. Where an offence is committed after section 281(5) is in force, the maximum term is 51 weeks.
